variants.title: Heat capacity by relaxation: niobium through its transition
variants.sample: Niobium, a superconductor with Tc 9.25 K (SIMULATED)
variants.unknown: Sommerfeld coefficient, the jump at Tc
variants.note: Above Tc the normal-state C/T against T^2 gives gamma; below Tc the electronic part falls exponentially (here a gamma Tc exp(-b Tc/T), the phenomenological form of Corak et al. 1956 with a = 9.17, b = 1.5, quoted from memory - verify) and the jump at Tc is the transition anomaly. gamma = 7.79 mJ/(mol K^2), ThD = 275 K and Tc from Kittel's tables.

source.title: C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, Tables 6.3 and 10.1: niobium

variants.title: Heat capacity by relaxation: a Schottky anomaly in an insulator
variants.sample: Magnetic insulator with a two-level crystal-field doublet (SIMULATED)
variants.note: No conduction electrons: the lattice gives beta T^3 and a split ground doublet the Schottky peak R (D/T)^2 e^(D/T)/(1 + e^(D/T))^2, largest near 0.42 D. A least-squares fit of both terms gives the gap D in kelvin. The gap and Debye temperature are illustrative.

source.title: Kittel, ch. 14: the Schottky anomaly of a two-level system
source.note: the sample's gap and Debye temperature are illustrative
